scores.evidence: No layout failures on any screen. The s4-sort mermaid flowchart (flowchart TD) has readable Japanese labels at 390 px (pages/mobile-jp-17.png, pages/mobile-jp-18.png), and the code, prompt, steps, quiz and checklist blocks all render cleanly. Two small things hold it back. Steps titles repeat the number, so the reader's circle 1 sits next to the title's ① (s3-steps, p-steps). Inline backticks show up as raw characters inside the prompt bodies (s3-prompt-write, s3-prompt-green, s2-goal-prompt, p-prompt-write, p-prompt-green, p-prompt-review).

The page has a steady rhythm: definitions, prompt, code, callout and quiz blocks alternate with short paragraphs, and there are no walls of text in desktop-jp.png. Only one mobile screen counts as text-only (mobile-jp-04, the s1-table list right after the s1-defs card), and desktop has none.

Everything is in Japanese, including the diagram labels, the reader chrome and the prompt variable chips. There is no stray English UI text, and no Japanese word is broken mid-word. Body text has good contrast. Nothing is hidden under the mobile top or bottom bars, and the 答える and この予想で決定 buttons are visible on every quiz.

niceToHave: s3-steps / p-steps: each step title starts with ①–⑧, but the reader already draws a numbered circle beside it, so learners see '1 ① テストと空の関数を…' (pages/mobile-jp-10.png, pages/mobile-jp-23.png). Consider dropping the circled number from the title. Keep the '（①の依頼文）' / '（依頼文1）' cross-references, or put them in the prompt titles only.

s3-prompt-write / s3-prompt-green / s2-goal-prompt / p-prompt-write / p-prompt-green / p-prompt-review: prompt bodies show literal backticks (`isPostalCode`, `node:test`, `isLeapYear`, /goal `node --test`) as plain characters (pages/mobile-jp-12.png, pages/mobile-jp-08.png, pages/desktop-jp-08.png). They are fine in what Claude receives, but they look like leaked markup. Consider using 「」 quotes for names in the Japanese prose, or keep them on purpose.

s3-code / p-model-code: at 390 px, the long lines (`'node:assert/strict'`, `'./postal.mjs'`, the end of the test('…') lines) run past the right edge of the code block (pages/mobile-jp-12.png, pages/mobile-jp-13.png, pages/mobile-jp-29.png). The block scrolls horizontally, so nothing is lost. Shorter test names (for example test('ハイフンなし', …)) would show more without scrolling.

reader: inline code breaks in the middle of a token at line ends: '/code-' | 'review' in s4-names (pages/mobile-jp-18.png) and '/output-' | 'style learning' in s5-defs (pages/desktop-jp-14.png). A no-break rule for short inline code would help.
reader: desktop JP charsPerLine median is 40, at the top of the 30–40 target, and the max is 49.

reader (known): the mobile full-length PNG stops at 16000 px, failed /api/ requests are ignored, and the end banner says this is the course's last lesson because drafts are not in course.json (pages/mobile-jp-38.png, pages/desktop-jp-25.png). There is also no scroll cue on wide code blocks.
summary: metrics.json is clean: overflowX false, 0 console, mermaid, unknown-block or broken-image errors. Every mobile-jp and desktop-jp screen renders without clipping, overlap or privacy problems, and the TD flowchart stays readable at 390 px. Only cosmetic polish is left: the doubled step numbering (circle plus ①) and raw backticks in prompt bodies, both under niceToHave.
